title: Leaving Buckinghamshire: The First Step
text: From the quiet country lanes of Buckinghamshire in the Chiltern Hills, Bryn straps on his pack and sets foot on the 2,000 km hike. The morning mist over the beech woodlands marks the commencement of months of walking.

title: The White Cliffs of Dover
text: Walking along the historic North Downs Way through Canterbury towards Dover. Looking out over the English Channel from the iconic chalk cliffs before boarding the ferry to the European continent.

title: Touching Down in France: Calais & Picardy
text: Stepping onto French soil at Calais. Joining the official Via Francigena, winding through pastoral farmland, quiet canals, and historic towns across the Nord-Pas-de-Calais and Picardy.

title: Reims & The Champagne Hills
text: The towering Gothic spires of Notre-Dame de Reims greet the trail. Walking through miles of undulating vineyards and ancient chalk cellars in the heart of the world-famous Champagne region.

title: Ascending the Jura: Besançon
text: The terrain steepens as the trail hugs the Doubs River loop around Besançon's Citadel. Lush pine forests, limestone gorges, and crisp alpine air signal the transition toward the Swiss frontier.

title: Lake Geneva & The Lavaux Vineyards
text: Passing into Switzerland and descending onto the sapphire shores of Lake Geneva at Lausanne. Walking through UNESCO-listed terraced vineyards with the snow-capped Alps reflecting across the open water.

title: Conquering the Alps: Great St Bernard Pass
text: The pinnacle challenge of the entire journey: ascending to 2,469 meters (8,100 ft) into brisk mountain winds, snowfields, and the legendary 1,000-year-old hospice. Crossing the high alpine frontier into Italy.
location: Great St Bernard Pass, Swiss/Italian Border

title: Tuscan Trails: Lucca & Val d'Orcia
text: Descending from the Aosta Valley into the warm, golden light of Tuscany. Wandering along the Renaissance fortified walls of Lucca, cypress-lined gravel strade bianche, and olive orchards.

title: The Final Mile: Rome & St. Peter's Square
text: Entering Rome via Monte Mario to catch the very first awe-inspiring panoramic view of the Eternal City. Walking the final triumphal avenue into St. Peter's Square—2,050 kilometres on foot, dream fulfilled, and life-changing charities supported.
